Run cell-type-specific ExWAS

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/sc-exwas.R
run_sc_exwas.Rd

Performs pseudobulk differential expression analysis with a continuous exposure variable as covariate. Aggregates counts within each donor-celltype stratum to avoid pseudoreplication, then uses an empirical-Bayes pseudobulk model for inference.

Usage

run_sc_exwas(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExposomeExperiment'
run_sc_exwas(
  x,
  exposure,
  celltype_col = "cell_type",
  celltypes = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  min_cells = 10L,
  min_donors = 5L,
  filter_genes = TRUE,
  method = c("edgeR", "DESeq2", "voom_dream"),
  min_group_donors = 5L,
  filter_min_count = 10L,
  filter_min_total_count = 15L,
  filter_method = c("fixed_support", "filterByExpr"),
  filter_min_cpm = 1,
  filter_min_donors = 5L,
  test_features = NULL,
  robust = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A SingleCellExposomeExperiment. Each cell's donor is read from the colData column named by sampleColumn(x).

...

Must be empty. Any further argument is an error, so that a misspelled argument name cannot silently change the analysis.

exposure

Character. Name of the exposure variable (column in exposureData).

celltype_col

Character. Column in colData containing cell type annotations. Default "cell_type".

celltypes

Character vector (optional). Which cell types to test. Default: all.

covariates

Character vector (optional). Additional covariates from exposureData. A covariate cannot be called "exposure", the name of the model's exposure term, or be the exposure itself, and each name must be a syntactic R name (see make.names) because it goes into the model formula; ., ... and names such as ..1, which R reads specially there, cannot be used.

min_cells

Integer. Minimum cells per donor-celltype stratum. Default 10.

min_donors

Integer. Minimum donors per cell type. Default 5, and at least 3, for every backend. Cell types with fewer valid donors are skipped with a warning.

filter_genes

Logical. If TRUE (default), filter low-expression genes before model fitting. The edgeR backend defaults to exposure-label-independent donor-support filtering; the DESeq2 and voom-dream backends retain genes detected in at least 20% of donors. If FALSE, every backend leaves out, in each cell type, only the genes without any count in the donors analysed for it.

method

Character. Backend for differential expression. "edgeR" (default) uses the edgeR v4 quasi-likelihood pipeline (see Details). "DESeq2" uses DESeq2 on aggregated counts. "voom_dream" uses variancePartition's voomWithDreamWeights() and dream() with precision weights from the mean-variance trend (Hoffman and Roussos 2021). Pseudobulk data have one observation per donor and the model has no random effects, so dream() fits it with limma and the moderated t statistic uses the residual degrees of freedom. This backend does not use the dreamlet package.

min_group_donors

Integer. For a binary exposure, minimum complete donors required in each group for the edgeR backend, at least 2. Default 5.

filter_min_count

Numeric. Minimum count passed to edgeR::filterByExpr when filter_method = "filterByExpr".

filter_min_total_count

Numeric. Minimum total pseudobulk count for either edgeR filtering method.

filter_method

Character. edgeR expression-filtering rule. "fixed_support" (default) requires a fixed CPM threshold in a fixed number of independent donors and does not use exposure labels. "filterByExpr" retains the edgeR compatibility option.

filter_min_cpm

Numeric. CPM threshold for filter_method = "fixed_support". Default 1.

filter_min_donors

Integer. Minimum number of independent donors meeting filter_min_cpm. Default 5.

test_features

Optional character vector of feature identifiers that defines the reported hypothesis family. Library-size calculation, expression filtering, normalisation and dispersion estimation still use all available features; subsetting occurs only after model fitting. Every requested feature must pass the pre-specified expression filter in every tested cell type, otherwise the call fails rather than silently changing the requested hypothesis family. Currently supported only by the edgeR backend; other backends fail explicitly rather than ignoring it.

robust

Logical. For the edgeR backend, moderate the quasi-likelihood dispersions with robust empirical Bayes (glmQLFit(robust = TRUE)). Default TRUE.

Value

A DataFrame with one row per tested gene and cell type and the same columns, in the same order, for every backend: gene, celltype, log2FC, se, statistic, pvalue, pvalue_underflow_clamped (TRUE where a p-value of exactly zero was replaced by the smallest positive double), padj (BH within the cell type), padj_global (BH across all tested gene-by-cell-type hypotheses), logCPM, exposure, n_donors, n_unexposed and n_exposed (group sizes when the exposure takes two values, otherwise NA), min_cells and median_cells (cells per donor in the cell type), and method. Rows are ordered by padj_global, then pvalue.

logCPM is the average log2 count per million reported by the backend: edgeR's logCPM for the edgeR backend, the mean of the voom log-CPM values for voom-dream, and edgeR::aveLogCPM() of the filtered pseudobulk counts for DESeq2.

Uncertainty fields are backend-specific: edgeR QL reports se as numeric NA and statistic as the directional signed square root of the QL F statistic; DESeq2 reports its coefficient standard error and Wald statistic; voom-dream reports the moderated standard error (|log2FC / t|) and the moderated t statistic. metadata(result)$parameters records the settings, the backend and its package version, se_method and statistic_type; metadata(result)$diagnostics holds, for each fitted cell type, the donors used, the numbers of genes before and after filtering and the design columns; for the edgeR backend also dropped_design_columns, the covariate columns left out of the design as collinear (each is also reported in a warning), and residual_df, the smallest adjusted residual degrees of freedom over the fitted genes (df.residual.adj).

Details

The pseudobulk approach aggregates single-cell counts within each (donor x cell type) stratum, creating one observation per donor per cell type. This correctly treats cells from the same donor as non-independent, avoiding the inflated Type I error rates that plague cell-level analyses (Squair et al. 2021, Nat Commun). The pseudobulk counts that enter the models are available as SummarizedExperiment objects from donor_pseudobulk.

The exposure variable and specified covariates enter one donor-level design matrix. The default edgeR backend fits the edgeR v4 quasi-likelihood model, glmQLFit(legacy = FALSE), which sets the negative-binomial dispersion internally from the most highly expressed genes and moderates the quasi-likelihood dispersions by empirical Bayes; the exposure coefficient is tested with a quasi-likelihood F-test (Chen et al. 2025). No separate estimateDisp() step is run: from edgeR 4.10.0 the method gives the same result whether or not the data hold such estimates, whereas earlier edgeR 4.x releases did not. The edgeR version and legacy = FALSE are recorded in metadata(result)$parameters. Complete-transcriptome library sizes are retained when expression filtering or test_features restricts the reported hypothesis family.

edgeR::glmQLFTest does not return a coefficient standard error. Consequently, the edgeR backend never reconstructs se from the ratio of the log-fold change to the QL statistic. Its statistic field is a directional ranking representation of the QL F statistic, not a Wald z or t statistic, and must not be used to derive a coefficient confidence interval. The edgeR result metadata records se_method = "not_available_edgeR_QL" and statistic_type = "signed_sqrt_qlf".

What is delegated and what is kept. The raw counts of each donor and cell type are summed with scrapper::aggregateAcrossCells(), and the models are fitted by edgeR, DESeq2 or variancePartition and limma. Four choices are made by exposomeSC itself, on purpose, because they define the hypotheses of an exposome-wide study:

  1. The exposure is a donor-level variable from exposureData(x), continuous or binary, and enters the design matrix together with the covariates; cells are never grouped by exposure.

  2. Gene filtering does not use the exposure. The default edgeR rule (filter_method = "fixed_support") keeps genes with at least filter_min_cpm CPM in filter_min_donors donors, and the DESeq2 and voom-dream backends keep genes detected in at least 20% of donors (and in at least two); which genes are tested therefore does not depend on the exposure values. By contrast, scran::pseudoBulkDGE(), for example, filters each label with edgeR::filterByExpr() using the design matrix.

  3. In the edgeR backend the library sizes are the column sums of the complete pseudobulk transcriptome, computed before filtering, and are kept when filtering or test_features reduces the tested genes. The voom-dream backend computes library sizes from the retained genes and DESeq2 uses its own size factors.

  4. padj_global applies the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure once across all tested gene-by-cell-type hypotheses, next to the within-cell-type padj.

References

Squair JW et al. (2021). Confronting false discoveries in single-cell differential expression. Nat Commun 12:5692. doi:10.1038/s41467-021-25960-2

Chen Y, Chen L, Lun ATL, Baldoni PL, Smyth GK (2025). edgeR v4: powerful differential analysis of sequencing data with expanded functionality and improved support for small counts and larger datasets. Nucleic Acids Research 53(2):gkaf018. doi:10.1093/nar/gkaf018

Hoffman GE, Roussos P (2021). Dream: powerful differential expression analysis for repeated measures designs. Bioinformatics 37(2):192–201. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa687

Hoffman GE, Schadt EE (2016). variancePartition: interpreting drivers of variation in complex gene expression studies. BMC Bioinformatics 17:483. doi:10.1186/s12859-016-1323-z

See also

donor_pseudobulk for the pseudobulk counts, run_multi_exwas for several exposures.

Examples

library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(S4Vectors)
set.seed(1)
counts <- matrix(rpois(5000, 8), nrow = 50,
    dimnames = list(paste0("G", 1:50), paste0("c", 1:100)))
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts = counts),
    colData = DataFrame(cell_id = paste0("c", 1:100),
        donor_id = rep(paste0("D", 1:5), each = 20),
        cell_type = rep(c("Mono", "NK"), 50)))
exp_mat <- matrix(rnorm(15), nrow = 5,
    dimnames = list(paste0("D", 1:5), c("E1", "E2", "E3")))
scee <- build_scee(sce, exp_mat, sample_col = "donor_id")
result <- run_sc_exwas(scee, exposure = "E1",
    celltype_col = "cell_type", min_cells = 5L)
head(result)
